subject: Request/Response schema decisions for Veridian integration
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@veridian.ai>, Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@veridian.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 23:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + schema decisions we need from Veridian

Hi Samir / Laura — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so engineering can start prototypes: 

Summary of asks we captured on the call:
- Primary goal: surface high-precision candidate passages from your internal docs, then rerank with context-aware scoring before presenting to end-users.
- Integration surface: Redwood will provide a small SDK and HTTP schema; your side will call Redwood endpoints for embeddings, rerank, and conversational generation.
- Important constraints you mentioned: 2k token average context, some single-shot API calls for batch scoring, and procurement timeline in mid-December.

Open schema decisions where we need preference from your engineers: 
1) Chat vs completions for the user-facing path — for multi-turn conversational UI we recommend chat (supports tool-calling/structured output); for single-shot rerank scoring of candidates, completions may be simpler and cheaper. Which do you prefer for the initial MVP?
2) Tokenization / max_tokens expectations — do you have a firm hard cap on response length or stop-sequence semantics we must match? You mentioned truncation is acceptable past 2.5k tokens.
3) Streaming semantics — would you prefer streaming partial tokens for perceived latency or full response only? (We can support both; streaming enables earlier UI render).
4) Structured tool calling — do you need JSON tool outputs (strict schema) or flexible text that we then parse?
5) Embeddings + reranker flow — confirm you want embedding-based candidate retrieval followed by an LR-style neural reranker vs returning raw embedding similarity scores.

Attachments: I attached a concise "redwood-schema-recs.pdf" with recommended request/response examples for chat and completions plus sample payloads.

Next steps:
- Samir/Laura: endorse one of the options above or note objections by EOD Monday (Dec 6).
- Redwood tech (Karthik/Marissa): prepare sample POST payloads and a short workshop once Veridian picks options.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake

jordan.blake@redwood.ai

From: Samir Patel <samir@veridian.ai>

Cc: Laura Cheng <laura.cheng@veridian.ai>, procurement@veridian.ai
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 23:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + schema decisions we need from Veridian

Thanks Jordan — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For the MVP we want the front-end conversational UI to be multi-turn, so chat sounds right. However, for batch candidate scoring (background job that scores 100–1000 candidate passages/ref hits) we want a minimal per-item payload (single-shot) and low cost. If using chat for batch scoring impacts cost, we'd prefer completions for that path.

- Token limits: we currently cap stored context to ~3k tokens on ingestion; user-visible responses should be under ~512 tokens ideally. Stop sequences: we have some legacy stop tokens used in our UI ("---END---"); can you make sure Redwood honors stop sequences in streaming?

- Streaming: we prefer streaming for the user-facing chat (progressive render), but for batch scoring we expect synchronous full responses.

- Structured output: For the tool-calling flow where Redwood can return a DB lookup action (eg: {"action":"lookup","id":"..."}), we want strict JSON so our orchestration layer can call downstream services deterministically.

We'll sync procurement on SLA questions after we confirm the technical flow. Can your team share a sample single-shot score API payload we can test with?

— Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Search & AI, Veridian Labs
samir@veridian.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: recommended schema split (chat vs completions) + token/streaming guidance

Internal note — based on Veridian's constraints, here's a recommended approach we should propose as the default in our next message: 

1) Two-path architecture (clear separation):
   - Chat endpoint (/v1/chat) for multi-turn UX + tool-calling / structured JSON outputs. Chat request uses messages[], system/user/assistant roles and supports function/tool schema. Streaming allowed with chunked JSON patches.
   - Completions endpoint (/v1/completions) for single-shot batch scoring and short generative outputs. Simpler payload (prompt + max_tokens), cheaper CPU/GPU path.

2) Tokenization / max_tokens:
   - Use byte-pair encoding tokenization (we support model-specific tokenizers). For the frontend chat, set default max_tokens=512; allow override to 1024 for longer replies. For batch scoring, set max_tokens small (16–64) because we only need a scalar scoring output or short rationale.

3) Stop sequences & streaming:
   - Implement honor_stop=true option in SDK. When streaming is enabled we emit partial tokens until the stop sequence is observed; on stop we send a final "stop" event and terminate the stream. If stop sequences are not found, stream closes at max_tokens.

4) Structured tool calling:
   - We recommend strict JSON schema for tool outputs (we provide JSON Schema files) and function calls for authoritative orchestration. Fallback: if the model returns plain text, we pass it through a safe parse step and emit a parse warning.

5) Embeddings + reranker:
   - Retrieval pipeline: embeddings for fast candidate retrieval (ANN), then a lightweight neural reranker (chat/completions style with context) to rescore top-K. For MVP K=50 is reasonable. Reranker should be single-shot completions with a scoring-only mode to reduce token cost.

Attachment: redwood-schema-recs.pdf (contains request/response examples and sample JSON Schema).

I'll draft a sample single-shot score payload for the Veridian team to run against a staging endpoint.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal: split chat/completions + sample payloads (attached)

Samir / Laura — following Karthik's note, our proposed defaults for the MVP: 

- Use /v1/chat for the conversational UI with streaming enabled and strict JSON tool calls for DB lookup actions.
- Use /v1/completions for batch candidate scoring (score-only mode; short max_tokens 16–64).
- Honor stop sequences in streaming (we expose honor_stop boolean).
- Embeddings retrieval -> completions-based reranker for top-K.

I've attached a short sample payload for the single-shot scoring endpoint (veridian-sample-payload.json) and the redwood-schema-recs.pdf with examples. If that looks good I'll have engineering spin up a staging endpoint and schedule a 90-minute workshop next Tue (Dec 8) to walk through the payloads and run smoke tests.

Action items: 
- Veridian: confirm the split (chat for UI, completions for scoring) and whether you want streaming for chat.
- Redwood: stand up staging endpoints and prepare an SDK snippet for auth (API key + optional mTLS).

Thanks — Jordan

Attachment: veridian-sample-payload.json (sample POST payloads)
